title: pH and Kw; Ka, pKa and Kb; pH of weak acids/bases; salt hydrolysis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AB02#t3 term and clue written for the game; AB02#t2 term and clue written for the game; AB02#t1 term and clue written for the game; AB02#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB02#N.4, AB05#N.5, AB06#N.3a, AB02#N.6, AB05#N.6, AB06#N.4, AB02#N.10a, AB05#N.13a, AB06#N.15a, AB02#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neutral solution
items.clue: An aqueous mixture in which [H⁺] equals [OH⁻].

items.label: Universal indicator
items.clue: Paper or liquid matched against a chart to estimate pH to about 1 unit.

items.label: pH meter
items.clue: Gives a precise reading, usually to 0.01, after being calibrated with buffers.

items.label: Kw
items.clue: The fixed product [H⁺] × [OH⁻]: if one concentration rises tenfold, the other falls tenfold.

questions.stem: Hydrobromic acid, HBr, is a strong acid. What is the pH of 4.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ HBr(aq)?
questions.explanation: HBr ionises completely, so [H⁺] = 4.0 × 10⁻³ and pH = −log₁₀(4.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.40.

questions.stem: Benzoic acid has pKa = 4.20. What is its Ka?
questions.explanation: Ka = 10⁻⁴·²⁰ = 6.3 × 10⁻⁵. Sense check: pKa between 4 and 5, so Ka between 10⁻⁵ and 10⁻⁴.

questions.stem: What is the pH of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH(aq), at 298 K? Ka = 1.74 × 10⁻⁵. Assume that the equilibrium concentration of CH₃COOH equals its initial concentration.
A student needs the pH of a solution. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Universal indicator gives the pH to two decimal places if the colour is matched carefully.
A pH meter calibrated with buffers of known pH gives a reading to about 0.01 unit.
A pH meter needs no calibration, as its reading is electronic.
Universal indicator is a single indicator that changes colour only at pH 7.

questions.explanation: Calibrated against buffers, a pH meter gives a precise numerical reading, usually to 0.01. Universal indicator only estimates pH.

questions.stem: At 298 K the pKa of methanoic acid, HCOOH, is 3.75 and the pKa of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, is 4.76. Which statement about 0.10 mol dm⁻³ solutions of the two acids is correct?

options.text: Ethanoic acid is the stronger acid, as its pKa is the larger.
Both are dissociated to the same extent, as both are weak acids.
Methanoic acid needs more NaOH(aq) to neutralise the same volume of it.
Methanoic acid is dissociated to a greater extent than ethanoic acid.

questions.explanation: The smaller pKa means the larger Ka (1.8 × 10⁻⁴ against 1.7 × 10⁻⁵), so methanoic acid is stronger and more dissociated at the same concentration.

questions.stem: A 0.20 mol dm⁻³ solution of a weak acid, HA, has pH 2.70 at 298 K. What is Ka?
At 298 K, solution P has [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ and solution Q has [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. Kw = 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol² dm⁻⁶. How does [OH⁻] in P compare with [OH⁻] in Q?

options.text: It is 100 times larger in P than in Q.
It is the same, as acid has no effect on [OH⁻].
Neither contains OH⁻ ions, as both are acidic.
It is 100 times smaller in P than in Q.

questions.explanation: [OH⁻] = Kw/[H⁺]: P 1.0 × 10⁻¹¹, Q 1.0 × 10⁻⁹ mol dm⁻³. P has 100 times the [H⁺], so 1/100 of the [OH⁻].

questions.stem: What is the pH of pure water at this temperature, and is it neutral? At 323 K, Kw = 5.5 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol² dm⁻⁶.

options.text: pH 7.00; neutral
pH 6.63; acidic, as the pH is below 7
pH 6.63; neutral
pH 13.26; neutral

questions.explanation: [H⁺] = [OH⁻], so [H⁺] = √(5.5 × 10⁻¹⁴) = 2.35 × 10⁻⁷ and pH = 6.63. Neutral means [H⁺] = [OH⁻], whatever the pH.

questions.stem: Sodium benzoate, C₆H₅COONa, is a food preservative. Benzoic acid is a weak acid. A solution of sodium benzoate in pure water is alkaline. Which equation explains why?

options.text: C₆H₅COONa(s) → C₆H₅COO⁻(aq) + Na⁺(aq)
Na⁺(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NaOH(aq) + H⁺(aq)
C₆H₅COOH(aq) ⇌ C₆H₅COO⁻(aq) + H⁺(aq)
C₆H₅COO⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ C₆H₅COOH(aq) + OH⁻(aq)

questions.explanation: Benzoate is the conjugate base of a weak acid, so it takes H⁺ from water and leaves OH⁻. Only a small fraction reacts, so the solution is only mildly alkaline.

questions.stem: Two samples of rain are tested with a pH meter. Sample A has pH 4.2; sample B has pH 5.7. How does [H⁺] in sample A compare with [H⁺] in sample B?

options.text: It is 1.5 times greater, as the pH values differ by 1.5.
It is about 15 times greater: 10 times for each pH unit.
It is about 32 times greater.
It is about 32 times smaller, as sample A has the lower pH.

questions.explanation: [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ, so the ratio is 10⁻⁴·² ÷ 10⁻⁵·⁷ = 10¹·⁵ ≈ 32. Lower pH, more H⁺.
